character_facts: Othon von Salza is an ancestor in the central bloodline and has a pirate past.
Lady Edna is presented as beautiful, indomitable, and politically significant through her parentage.
Edna's fertility or lineage is treated as notable because she gave Othon only one son, Bari.
Baron Berard holds authority over Marmola and Castaka.
The Techno-Pope commands enough power or wealth to requisition vast quantities of marble.
characters_present: Othon von Salza (depicted or referenced in ancestral narration)
Baron Berard of Castaka (referenced in narration)
Bari (referenced as infant/son, not visibly shown)
continuity_links: This page continues the genealogical history of the Metabaron line by moving from Othon von Salza to his union with Edna and their son Bari.
It introduces Marmola and Castaka as the next important family setting in that lineage.
The unexpected arrival of the Imperial Merchants Guild ship sets up a likely conflict between Marmola's peaceful life and imperial extraction demands.
dialogue_meaning: The narration establishes a family link: Othon von Salza married into the ruling house of Marmola through Lady Edna.
It emphasizes a succession detail that Edna produced only one son, Bari.
The captions characterize Marmola as a marble planet with a small fertile valley supporting Castaka, living by exporting precious stone for imperial building works.
The dialogue frames Marmola as a resource target, with enough marble to pave Technogea and to build the Techno-Pope's new temple-bank.
The final remark revises the scale of extraction upward from a limited order to the removal of an entire mountain.
locations: A large interior structure or stair hall shown in inset, exact location unclear
lore_facts: Othon von Salza is described as the master's great-great-grandfather.
Othon was once an intergalactic pirate.
Lady Edna was the daughter of Baron Berard of Castaka.
Baron Berard is described as the undisputed ruler of Marmola in the Philorian system.
Marmola is a gigantic marble globe with only a small fertile valley housing the fortress of Castaka.
The Marmolans sustain themselves by selling precious marble to builders of imperial palaces.
Marmola had lived in tranquility until the arrival of a cargo ship from the Imperial Merchants Guild.
Technogea has streets that can be paved with Marmola's marble.
The Techno-Pope is building or planning a new temple-bank.
plot_events: The narration identifies Othon von Salza as an ancestor in the line being recounted.
The page states that Othon won the hand of Lady Edna, daughter of Baron Berard of Castaka and ruler of Marmola.
The narration says Edna bore Othon only one son, Bari.
The setting shifts to Marmola, described as a peaceful marble-producing world centered on Castaka.
A cargo ship from the Imperial Merchants Guild arrives unexpectedly at Marmola.
Observers aboard or near the ship assess Marmola as a vast source of marble for Technogea.
They conclude that the Techno-Pope's construction project will require far more marble than first suggested, up to an entire mountain.
uncertainties: The upper row of faces is not explicitly labeled panel-by-panel; it is unclear which face is meant to represent Othon or other ancestors.
Some wording in the top narration is small and slightly hard to read; details such as descriptive phrasing around Edna may not be perfectly transcribed.
The small inset stairway scene is visually present but its exact participants and location are not identified on the page.
The speaking characters in the lower scene are off-panel or not clearly singled out, so their identities are uncertain beyond being associated with the arriving ship or merchants.
visual_summary: The page combines genealogical narration with a new setting introduction. The top half shows a row of severe-looking figures in close-up against a starry backdrop, alongside a small inset of a monumental interior stairway with tiny people and cargo-like objects. Caption boxes explain the ancestry of Othon von Salza and Lady Edna, then describe the marble world Marmola and its fortress-valley of Castaka. The lower half is dominated by a large, detailed spacecraft looming over a gray spherical planet. Speech balloons from unseen or off-panel speakers describe the planet as a quarry rich in marble and estimate how much stone the Techno-Pope needs for a temple-bank, ending with the escalation that an entire mountain is required.
